article.title: Why Data Pipelines Need Idempotent Processing
article.why: 理解 retry、replay 與 duplicate side effect 的工程風險。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
Data pipelines rarely run in a perfectly clean environment. Networks time out, workers restart, APIs fail, schedulers trigger jobs twice, and operators rerun a failed day. Because retries are normal, a reliable pipeline should be designed so that processing the same logical input again does not create an unintended extra effect. This property is called idempotency.

Consider a daily transaction load. The pipeline reads 200,000 records, writes most of them to a warehouse, and then crashes before recording completion. An operator reruns the job. If the process simply inserts every row again, the warehouse may contain duplicates even though the source data did not change.

A common solution is to give each logical record a stable key. The destination can reject duplicates, perform an upsert, or replace a complete partition. Another pattern is to write into a staging table, validate counts and totals, and then swap the validated result into the production table.

Idempotency becomes more difficult when a pipeline creates external side effects. A database write can often be protected with a unique key, but sending an email, creating an invoice, charging a card, or publishing a message may happen outside the database. If the process crashes after the external action succeeds but before local state is updated, a retry can repeat the action.

For these cases, systems often use idempotency keys or request identifiers. The receiving service remembers that a logical request has already been processed and returns the previous result instead of performing the action again.

The correct unit of idempotency must also be defined. Is the unit one event, one customer-day, one source file, or one monthly partition? A key that is too broad can block valid updates. A key that is too narrow may still allow duplicate business effects.

Idempotent processing also makes backfills safer. Teams often need to recompute historical periods after a bug fix, logic change, or late-arriving data. If the pipeline converges to one expected state when the same period is processed repeatedly, engineers can rerun data with much less manual cleanup.

Testing should include replay scenarios, not only the happy path. Run the same input twice and compare row counts, sums, checksums, and downstream events. Kill a job after a partial write and retry it. Trigger the scheduler twice. These tests reveal assumptions that ordinary unit tests may miss.

It is important to distinguish idempotency from immutability. An idempotent operation may still update a record when the logical input has changed. The requirement is that replaying the same logical input should not create an additional unintended effect.

Operationally, idempotency reduces cognitive load. On-call staff do not need a special cleanup procedure every time a job is retried. Recovery becomes a routine action rather than a dangerous exception.

This is especially important in distributed systems because “exactly once” execution across databases, queues, APIs, and networks is difficult to guarantee. A more practical design is often “at least once delivery plus idempotent processing.”

The broader lesson is that retry behavior should be part of the original design, not an emergency patch added after the first incident. If a pipeline cannot answer the question “What happens if this step runs twice?”, it is not yet operationally mature. Good metadata helps too. Recording source batch IDs, processing timestamps, code versions, and row-level keys makes duplicate behavior easier to audit. When an incident occurs, teams can trace whether a result was produced once, replayed safely, or applied twice. Observability and idempotency reinforce each other: one prevents duplicate effects, while the other makes the execution history explainable.
paragraphs.zh: 可靠資料管線要假設 retry 一定會發生。相同 logical input 重跑時，不應產生額外重複紀錄、重複計費或其他 side effect。可用 stable key、upsert、staging、partition replacement 與 idempotency key 實作，並透過 replay test 驗證。
paragraphs.ja: 信頼できるデータパイプラインではretryを前提に設計します。同じ論理入力を再実行しても重複レコードや二重処理を生まないよう、stable key、upsert、staging、idempotency keyなどを使います。
